_: The four contracts ADR 0002 names as crossing the device/server boundary unchecked, written down once so both halves answer to the same file: server/internal/store/sync_contract_vectors_test.go and app/test/data/sync_contract_vectors_test.dart. Neither suite computes what it asserts. Change a name on one side only and both suites redden, which is the whole point — round B lost every prayer because each side asserted against its own implementation.

op_bodies._: Real op bodies, one per kind, exactly as a current device builds them. The server's decoder is DisallowUnknownFields, so one renamed or extra key is a refusal and a refusal is permanent: the write is dead-lettered and gone. The server suite lands each of these against a real Postgres and requires 'applied'; the device suite builds each body through the real write path and requires the same key set. Applied in this order — the kept item is deleted after it is kept.

op_results._: What the server can say about one op, and what the device must make of each answer. The device parks a permanent answer for the reader and retries everything else. Rename one of these words on the server and the device either retries a write that can never land or parks one that could have — and before this file, both suites stayed green.

change_kinds._: Every kind the change stream emits, with one row as the server builds it. The device must apply all of them: a kind it does not recognise is a table it silently stops writing, which is invisible on both sides. The server suite requires the stream to emit exactly these kinds with exactly these row keys; the device suite feeds each row through the real pull path and requires it to land.

reading_orders._: The two words, spelled once. They are an enum on the device and were a free string on the server, checked by nothing above the column constraint. A set id is derived from one of these words, so a third spelling is not a bad value but a set no other device can name.
